arms.predicted: Removing the periodic stream_synchronize at pipeline.rs:381 will increase cold lookup throughput consistently above the baseline mean of 3.87 GB/s, because eliminating the ~167 us sync stall removes a pipeline bubble where NVMe completions go unprocessed and the device command queue drains.
arms.observed: Baseline mean: 3.78 GB/s (3.76, 3.88, 3.69). Treatment mean: 3.76 GB/s (3.87, 3.43, 3.98). No consistent improvement — results are within run-to-run variance. The sync removal alone at QD16 with 2 streams produces no measurable throughput change. p99 latency: baseline avg 1259 us, treatment avg 1331 us (higher variance, not better).
arms.diagnostic_note: The GPU sync stall is NOT the bottleneck at QD16. With only 16 max in-flight NVMe reads and 32 chunks per 4 MiB object, the sliding window is already limited by the shallow NVMe queue. The sync fires once at stream_idx=16 (mid-object), but at QD16 the NVMe device is already underutilized — removing the sync doesn't help because there aren't enough in-flight reads to mask any stall. The bottleneck at QD16 is NVMe queue depth, not GPU sync. The sync stall (~167 us) is small relative to the NVMe read completion interval at shallow queues.

arms.predicted: Combining QD64 + 4 CUDA streams with removal of mid-transfer GPU sync will produce cold lookup throughput consistently above the iteration 1 best of 4.53 GB/s.
arms.observed: Treatment mean: 4.59 GB/s (4.51, 4.58, 4.68), consistently above iteration 1 best of 4.53 GB/s. p99 latency: avg 1081 us (down from baseline 1259 us). All 3 runs showed improvement over the baseline (3.78 GB/s) by +21% and over iter-1 best by +1.3%. Zero NVMe errors across all runs.
arms.diagnostic_note: The combined config (QD64 + 4 streams + sync removal) achieves 4.59 GB/s, which is above the iter-1 best of 4.53 GB/s but only marginally (+1.3%). Since h-main (sync removal alone) shows no improvement, and iter-1 achieved 4.53 GB/s with QD64+4 streams WITH the sync, the sync removal contributes at most ~1.3% improvement on top of QD64+4 streams. The dominant factor is queue depth + stream count, not sync elimination. The marginal gain may be within measurement noise.

arms.predicted: Changing the sync interval from 16 to 64 will produce cold lookup throughput matching h-main's improvement, because a 4 MiB object with 128 KiB chunks produces only 32 H2D copies — below the new 64-copy threshold — so no mid-object sync occurs.
arms.observed: Treatment mean: 3.90 GB/s (3.92, 3.87, 3.90). This matches baseline (3.78 GB/s) within variance — slightly higher but within noise. It matches h-main (3.76 GB/s) in that both show no meaningful improvement over baseline. Confirms that at QD16, eliminating mid-object sync (whether by removal or by raising the threshold) has no measurable effect.
arms.diagnostic_note: The prediction that h-robustness would match h-main is confirmed — both show no improvement. This confirms the sync is not the bottleneck at QD16. The prediction about matching an improvement was wrong because there was no improvement to match. However, the equivalence between full removal (h-main) and threshold increase (h-robustness) is validated.

discrepancy_analysis: The core hypothesis (GPU sync stalls are the bottleneck) is refuted at QD16/2-stream configuration. The sync stall does not create a meaningful pipeline bubble at low queue depths because the NVMe device is already underutilized with only 16 in-flight commands. The real bottleneck remains NVMe queue depth. The h-ablation result (4.59 GB/s) shows marginal improvement over iter-1's 4.53 GB/s when sync removal is combined with QD64+4 streams, but the effect is small (+1.3%) and may be within measurement noise. The dominant factor for throughput improvement remains deeper NVMe queues and more CUDA streams (as established in iter-1). Integrity check fails identically on all conditions including baseline (pre-existing issue in verification harness, not related to our changes).
